prompt: Darcy has two part-time jobs during her summer vacation: counselor at a local day camp and lifeguard at the community swimming pool. Darcy works a combined total of 40 hours every week between the two jobs. The first week working both jobs, it rained all but one day, so three-fourths of the hours she worked that week were at the day camp. How many hours did Darcy work at the pool the first week?

solutions.title: Remaining fraction
solutions.body:
The pool got $1 - \frac34 = \frac14$ of the hours: $\frac14 \times 40 = 10$ hours.

**Answer: 10 hours**

prompt: Darcy has two part-time jobs during her summer vacation: counselor at a local day camp and lifeguard at the community swimming pool. Darcy works a combined total of 40 hours every week between the two jobs. The second week, the number of hours Darcy worked at the day camp was $\frac35$ the number of hours she worked at the swimming pool. What is the positive difference in the number of hours Darcy worked at the day camp and the number of hours she worked at the pool during the second week?

solutions.title: Ratio parts
solutions.body:
Camp : pool $= 3 : 5$, which is 8 parts for 40 hours, so 1 part $= 5$ hours. Camp 15, pool 25; difference $10$ hours.

**Answer: 10 hours**

prompt: Darcy has two part-time jobs during her summer vacation: counselor at a local day camp and lifeguard at the community swimming pool. Darcy works a combined total of 40 hours every week between the two jobs. In the first week, three-fourths of her hours were at the day camp. In the second week, her day-camp hours were $\frac35$ of her pool hours. Darcy earns \$8 per hour as a camp counselor and \$12 per hour as a lifeguard. What is the positive difference in the amount Darcy earned the first week and the amount she earned the second week?

solutions.title: Only the shift matters
solutions.body:
From week 1 to week 2, 15 hours moved from camp to pool (pool went from 10 to 25). Each moved hour pays $12 - 8 = 4$ dollars more: $15 \times 4 = 60$.

**Answer: \$60**

prompt: Darcy has two part-time jobs during her summer vacation: counselor at a local day camp and lifeguard at the community swimming pool. Darcy works a combined total of 40 hours every week between the two jobs. Darcy earns \$8 per hour as a camp counselor and \$12 per hour as a lifeguard. What is the total amount Darcy will earn during the third week if she earns the same amount working at the day camp as she earns working at the pool?

solutions.title: Set the earnings equal
solutions.body:
$8d = 12p$ gives $d = \frac32 p$. Then $\frac32 p + p = 40$, so $p = 16$ and $d = 24$. Each job pays $12 \times 16 = 192$, total $384$ dollars.

**Answer: \$384**

solutions.title: Inverse ratio
solutions.body:
Equal pay means hours are in the inverse ratio of wages: camp : pool $= 12 : 8 = 3 : 2$, so 24 h and 16 h. Earnings: $8(24) + 12(16) = 192 + 192 = 384$.

**Answer: \$384**
